gen-dafont-groovy-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Groovy squeezes its c down to a narrow slit and spaces its lowercase loosely, with arms and legs of constant width. Schibsted Grotesk is the opposite, a plain sans with big open e and a shapes, and a headline in Groovy can go large without it crowding.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-sen: Groovy draws its c almost shut, with loose lowercase spacing and arms and legs of constant width, funky and friendly at once. Sen stands tall and open beneath it, tracing every curve with a single steady line.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-sintony: Groovy gives its c just a narrow slit and spaces the lowercase loosely, so every arm and leg carries the same visual mass. And Sintony, a sans-serif with a chunky, tall midzone, keeps long paragraphs smooth, with no curve clogging up.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-sofia-sans: Funky and tightly drawn, Groovy nearly seals its c and lets its loose lowercase run on arms and legs of constant width. And Sofia Sans, a sans-serif of tall, open-sided rounds, would feel oversized and stencil-like if you blew it up for the body.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-stack-sans-notch: Funky, loose-limbed lowercase with a c that nearly closes: that is Groovy. And Stack Sans Notch, a plain sans with open curves like rod stock, leaves the shouting to Groovy, which earns its keep when big and short.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-stack-sans-text: Groovy pinches its c down to a slit and spaces its lowercase loosely, all in arms and legs of constant width. But Stack Sans Text, a sans with big-bodied lowercase and marker-like lines, keeps its curve endings well apart and does the quiet work of reading.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-sulphur-point: Groovy's c nearly closes into a narrow slit, and its loosely tracked lowercase has arms and legs of constant width. Sulphur Point, a sans with open gaps and bulky lowercase, would carry a long read in a steady marker-like line.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-tiktok-sans: TikTok Sans reads big and open, its x-height rising close to cap height. Groovy, with its nearly closed c and loose, funky lowercase, takes the front while the sans-serif below stays spacious and easy to follow.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-ubuntu-sans: Groovy leaves only a narrow slit in its c, and its lowercase spreads loosely. Its heading letters stay closed and funky, while Ubuntu Sans, a sans-serif with washer-sized eyes and tubular strokes, keeps its loops open and lets the text breathe.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-vend-sans: Friendly and a little funky, Groovy pulls its c almost shut and spaces its lowercase loosely. And Vend Sans, a sans-serif drawn with a ruler-straight line and wide, unclosed terminals, fills the line below with open, upright text.
